approved_input.value: Visual and Patient-Reported Outcomes after Mix-and-Match Implantation of an Extended Depth of Focus and a Trifocal Intraocular Lens

The TECNIS Odyssey is a new full range of vision IOL, with current reports suggests high visual acuity and spectacle independence at distance, intermediate, and near.1,2

The TECNIS PureSee is a new non-diffractive extended depth of focus (EDOF) IOL. The non-diffractive design may reduce reports of dysphotopsias and improve contrast sensitivity compared to diffractive IOLs. A large randomized control trial suggesting better intermediate and near vision with the PureSee IOL, compared to a monofocal control, and similar contrast sensitivity, distance vision, and dysphotopsia profile.3

Mix-and-match implantation of an EDOF IOL in the dominant eye and multifocal IOL in the non-dominant eye may enable better range of vision and fewer visual disturbances compared to bilateral implantation of the EDOF or trifocal IOLs alone.
To date there are minimal data on visual outcomes, patient satisfaction, and patient-reported dysphotopsias using mix-and-match implantation of the PureSee (dominant eye) and the Odyssey (non-dominant eye).
1. Hacopian AG, Brunson PB, Hall B. Patient Reported Outcomes and Visual Acuity After Bilateral Implantation of a Next Generation Presbyopia Correcting Intraocular Lens. OPTH. 2026;20:1-8. doi:10.2147/OPTH.S572703
2. Bissen-Miyajima H, Midorikawa M, Fujisaki R, Ota Y, Minami K, Honda R. Early Clinical Results of a Newly Developed Continuous Range of Vision Intraocular Lens. Ophthalmol Ther. 2025;14(11):2937-2945. doi:10.1007/s40123-025-01235-7
3.  Corbett D, Black D, Roberts TV, Cronin B, Gunn D, Bala C, Versace P, Tsai L, Papadatou E, Alarcon A, Vilupuru S. Quality of vision clinical outcomes for a new fully-refractive extended depth of focus Intraocular Lens. Eye. 2024;38(S1):9-14. doi:10.1038/s41433-024-03039-8

The hypothesis is that mix-and-match implantation of the PureSee and Odyssey intraocular lenses (IOLs) will result in excellent visual outcomes at distance, intermediate, and near, high patient satisfaction, and low reports of visual disturbances.

The TECNIS PureSee is a new non-diffractive extended depth of focus (EDOF) IOL. The non-diffractive design may reduce reports of dysphotopsias and improve contrast sensitivity compared to diffractive IOLs. A large randomized control trial suggesting better intermediate and near vision with the PureSee IOL, compared to a monofocal control, and similar contrast sensitivity, distance vision, and dysphotopsia profile.3

Mix-and-match implantation of an EDOF IOL in the dominant eye and multifocal IOL in the non-dominant eye may enable better range of vision and fewer visual disturbances compared to bilateral implantation of the EDOF or trifocal IOLs alone.
To date there are minimal data on visual outcomes, patient satisfaction, and patient-reported dysphotopsias using mix-and-match implantation of the PureSee (dominant eye) and the Odyssey (non-dominant eye).
1. Hacopian AG, Brunson PB, Hall B. Patient Reported Outcomes and Visual Acuity After Bilateral Implantation of a Next Generation Presbyopia Correcting Intraocular Lens. OPTH. 2026;20:1-8. doi:10.2147/OPTH.S572703
2. Bissen-Miyajima H, Midorikawa M, Fujisaki R, Ota Y, Minami K, Honda R. Early Clinical Results of a Newly Developed Continuous Range of Vision Intraocular Lens. Ophthalmol Ther. 2025;14(11):2937-2945. doi:10.1007/s40123-025-01235-7

approved_input.value: Visual and Patient-Reported Outcomes after Mix-and-Match Implantation of an Extended Depth of Focus and a Trifocal Intraocular Lens

The TECNIS Odyssey is a new full range of vision IOL, with current reports suggests high visual acuity and spectacle independence at distance, intermediate, and near.1,2

The TECNIS PureSee is a new non-diffractive extended depth of focus (EDOF) IOL. The non-diffractive design may reduce reports of dysphotopsias and improve contrast sensitivity compared to diffractive IOLs. A large randomized control trial suggesting better intermediate and near vision with the PureSee IOL, compared to a monofocal control, and similar contrast sensitivity, distance vision, and dysphotopsia profile.3

Mix-and-match implantation of an EDOF IOL in the dominant eye and multifocal IOL in the non-dominant eye may enable better range of vision and fewer visual disturbances compared to bilateral implantation of the EDOF or trifocal IOLs alone.
To date there are minimal data on visual outcomes, patient satisfaction, and patient-reported dysphotopsias using mix-and-match implantation of the PureSee (dominant eye) and the Odyssey (non-dominant eye).

The hypothesis is that mix-and-match implantation of the PureSee and Odyssey intraocular lenses (IOLs) will result in excellent visual outcomes at distance, intermediate, and near, high patient satisfaction, and low reports of visual disturbances.

paragraphs.text: No inferential hypothesis test is planned for this descriptive observational study.
The analysis population will include participants who complete the Month 3 postoperative assessment and have evaluable outcome data.

For the primary and secondary continuous visual-acuity outcomes and the secondary defocus-curve outcome grouped in Study Design, descriptive summaries will report sample size, mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, and maximum. Responses to each AIOLIS questionnaire question, also specified among the secondary endpoints in Study Design, will be summarized by response category using counts and percentages.

Adverse events and device deficiencies will be described by event category, seriousness, severity, relationship, action taken, and outcome. No inferential hypothesis test is planned for this descriptive observational study.
Study results may be presented or published only in a form that protects participant confidentiality and follows the approved publication and data-governance requirements.

Study records will use appropriate identifiers and access controls. Identifiable information will be available only to authorized personnel and oversight bodies as permitted by the approved protocol and applicable law.
The planned participant follow-up period is 3 months. Completion of follow-up is distinct from early discontinuation of participation.

A participant may discontinue participation at any time without penalty or loss of benefits to which the participant is otherwise entitled. The study team may document the reason when the participant chooses to provide one, and information collected before withdrawal may continue to be used as permitted by the consent and applicable requirements.
The study timeline provides 6 months for enrollment, 3 months for follow-up, and 1 month for data analysis.
Confidentiality protections for study records and participant information are described in Section 16.
The Schedule of Assessments presents the study procedures and their timing across preoperative screening, the operative visits, and the 3-month postoperative evaluation.
No compensation or reimbursement will be provided to participants for study participation.

Participants who believe that a study activity caused an injury or medical problem should contact the study doctor promptly and seek emergency care when needed. TECNIS Odyssey and TECNIS PureSee are artificial lenses placed inside the eye. Odyssey is designed to provide vision over a full range of distances. Reports about Odyssey suggest clear vision and less need for glasses for distance, middle-distance and near tasks.

PureSee is an extended depth of focus lens, designed to extend the range over which objects appear in focus. It has a non-diffractive design, meaning it does not use diffraction to spread light into different focuses. This design may reduce unwanted visual effects and improve the ability to distinguish objects from their background compared with lenses that use diffraction. A large randomized trial suggested that PureSee provided better middle-distance and near vision than a monofocal lens, which focuses at one distance. That trial also suggested similar distance vision, ability to distinguish objects from their background, and unwanted visual effects.

The mix-and-match approach uses lenses with different focusing designs in the two eyes. Here, PureSee is used in the dominant eye, the eye preferred for viewing, and Odyssey in the non-dominant eye. There is little information about vision, satisfaction and unwanted visual effects with this particular pairing. This evidence gap is the reason for studying the combination.

This study is for adults undergoing surgery for age-related cataracts. You cannot join if your surgeon considers you to have a moderate or severe condition that could increase the risk of complicated cataract surgery. At the preoperative screening visit, the study team will go through informed consent with you and collect your demographic information and medical history. At the 3-month postoperative visit, your vision will be tested with both eyes together under bright-light conditions. Tests will measure distance vision, intermediate vision at 66 cm, and near vision at 40 cm. Each distance will be tested both without correction and with correction for distance vision. A distance-corrected defocus curve will also be measured to assess vision across a range of focus. These are measurements of vision, not treatments.

At that follow-up visit, you will also complete the AIOLIS questionnaire. The study team will monitor for adverse events, meaning health problems, and device deficiencies, meaning problems with the lenses. An exit form will be completed.

The purpose is to evaluate vision and patients' experiences after mix-and-match implantation of PureSee and Odyssey intraocular lenses. The researchers' hypothesis is that this approach will produce excellent vision at far, middle and near distances, high patient satisfaction and few visual disturbances. This is an expectation being tested, not an assured result.

The primary endpoint, or main outcome, is binocular distance-corrected intermediate visual acuity at 66 cm, measured 3 months after surgery. This means how clearly you can see at that middle distance using both eyes together while wearing correction for distance vision.

In cataract surgery, intraocular lenses (IOLs) that extend the range of vision are being evaluated for visual performance, spectacle independence, and visual disturbances. TECNIS Odyssey is a new full-range-of-vision IOL; reports by Hacopian and colleagues (2026) and Bissen-Miyajima and colleagues (2025) suggest high visual acuity and spectacle independence at distance, intermediate, and near. TECNIS PureSee is a new non-diffractive extended depth of focus (EDOF) IOL. Its non-diffractive design may reduce dysphotopsias and improve contrast sensitivity compared with diffractive IOLs. A large randomized controlled trial reported by Corbett and colleagues (2024) suggests better intermediate and near vision with PureSee than with a monofocal control, with similar contrast sensitivity, distance vision, and dysphotopsia profiles. However, data remain limited on visual outcomes, patient satisfaction, and patient-reported dysphotopsias following mix-and-match implantation of PureSee in the dominant eye and Odyssey in the non-dominant eye. This evidence gap motivates evaluation of the combined approach.

The objective is to evaluate whether mix-and-match implantation of PureSee and Odyssey IOLs results in excellent distance, intermediate, and near visual outcomes, high patient satisfaction, and low reports of visual disturbances.

study.title: Visual and Patient-Reported Outcomes after Mix-and-Match Implantation of an Extended Depth of Focus and a Trifocal Intraocular Lens
study.background:
The TECNIS Odyssey is a new full range of vision IOL, with current reports suggests high visual acuity and spectacle independence at distance, intermediate, and near.1,2

The TECNIS PureSee is a new non-diffractive extended depth of focus (EDOF) IOL. The non-diffractive design may reduce reports of dysphotopsias and improve contrast sensitivity compared to diffractive IOLs. A large randomized control trial suggesting better intermediate and near vision with the PureSee IOL, compared to a monofocal control, and similar contrast sensitivity, distance vision, and dysphotopsia profile.3

Mix-and-match implantation of an EDOF IOL in the dominant eye and multifocal IOL in the non-dominant eye may enable better range of vision and fewer visual disturbances compared to bilateral implantation of the EDOF or trifocal IOLs alone.
To date there are minimal data on visual outcomes, patient satisfaction, and patient-reported dysphotopsias using mix-and-match implantation of the PureSee (dominant eye) and the Odyssey (non-dominant eye).
